caseno: Appeal from Original order No. 171 of 1984.
lawyer:
Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed ----- for the appellant. 
Fakir Abdul Mannan with Zakir Ahmed ----- for the respondents.
parties:
Chowdhury Saifuddin Ahmed ------ Appellant 
vs.  
Shamsuddin & Ors ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Title Suit No. 322 of 1977 was filed by the plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1-8 against the appellant and others as defendants for partition of the partiable properties in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. The suit was fixed for ex parte hearing on 16.7.80. The appellant being defendant No. 26 was out of the country on a visit to the U.S.A. from 25.6.80. He could not take any steps, nor could he instruct his learned Advocate. In such circumstances the suit was decreed ex parte on 16.7.80. His learned Advocate, owing to inadvertence, pursued the cause list of Title Suit No. 322 of 1980 and mistakenly noted in his diary that the title suit in question was fixed for hearing on 18.8.80 and there aft 28.9.80. When he found on 28.9.80 that the s was set down for solenama, it aroused his suspicion and so he looked for the records of Tide Suit No. 322 of 1977, but the same could not be traced and the annual vacation came about within a few days. In the meanwhile the appellant returned from U.S.A. on 7.9.80. His only son died in a road accident on 27.9.80. For full two months thereafter he was not in a mental state to take any steps in worldly affairs. After re-opening of the Court his learned Advocate traced or the records of Title Suit No. 322 of 1977 and came to learn for the first time on 20.11.80 that the suit was decreed ex parte on 16.7.80. This information was communicated to the appellant on 23.11.80. Thereafter, the appellant filed the miscellaneous case on 20.12.80. The appellant prayed that his application be registered and after hearing the parties the ex parte decree dated 16.7.80 be set aside. 

 3. The plaintiff-respondents contested the miscellaneous case by filing a written objection in which they contended that the application was not maintainable in the present form, that it was bad for defect of parties, that it was barred by limitation and that it was made only to harass and deprive the respondents of the fruit of the decree. It was stated that the appellant entered appearance in the suit in 1977 and obtained adjournment for three years on various pretexts to file written statement. When he failed to do so, the suit was fixed for ex parte hearing and even the ex parte hearings were adjourned from time to time upon the prayer of the appellant. Finally, the suit was decreed ex parte on 16.7.80. Thereafter a Pleader Commissioner was appointed who surveyed the suit properties and submitted his report but the appellant did not file any objection and the report of the Pleader Commissioner has been accepted and final decree has been passed in the partition suit. The bonafide mistake of the learned Advocate for the appellant was not a bonafide one. The plaintiff-respondents also filed an additional written objection and contended that the appellant has no longer any locus standi to file the miscellaneous case, because he has already divested himself of his entire interest in the suit properties. The respondents also vigorously denied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing or that the delay in filing the miscellaneous case was unintentional. They contended that the ellaneous case was a malafide one and was filed with the object of harassing the respondents for unlawful gain. 

 7. It is admitted on all hands that in the present case the appellant has stated that the suit was decreed ex parte on 16.7.80 that he left for U.S.A. on 27.6.80 and returned to the country on 7.9.80. It is also admitted that he has explained what happened from 7.9.80 to 20.12.80 when he filed the miscellaneous case. It is strongly contended by the other side, however, that the appellant's account of what happened between 7.9.80 to 20.12.80 is patchy and disjointed, but that concerns the merit of the appellant's explanation. The point to note in this case is that without filing a separate application under section 5 of the Limitation Act the appellant has sought to explain in the application under Order 9, rule 13 itself as to why he was delayed in filing the miscellaneous case within the period of limitation of 30 days from the date of passing of the ex parte decree. Ii is also clear from the evidence on record that the appellant has examined himself as P.W.1 and his learned Advocate Mr. Syed Altaf Hossain as P.W.2 and that they have sought to explain the happenings from 7.9.80 to 20.12.80 in their respective evidence. It is also on record that the plaintiff-respondents by examining one witness, O,P.W.1 Kamaluddin, have seriously disputed the appellant's contentions regarding the happenings between 7.9.80 to 20.12.80. 

 15. The appellant as P.W.1 Visa cross-examined in detail and from his cross-examination we find that he entered appearance in me suit in 1977 and he took time for more than three years to file a written statement On 23.11.79 the court granted time to me a written statement as a last chance, in default fixed the suit for ex parte hearing on 22.12.79. Thereafter the ex parte hearing was fixed on 18.2.80, 17.3;80, 17.4. 80, 27.5.80 and 16.5.80. P.W.l has admitted that on 16.6.80 he again applied for time but the prayer was rejected and 16.7.80 was fixed for ex parte disposal. 

 16. It is the appellant's case that he left for U.S.A on 21.6.80 and, therefore could not take any steps on the date of hearing. But it is clear from his cross-examination that 16.7.80 was fixed as the date for ex parte disposal in his presence and within his knowledge. Therefore, it is pertinent to inquire as to what steps he took before he left for U.S.A. so that the hearing on 16.7.80 is taken care of. Nothing has been said to that effect in me application under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In his evidence P.W.1 stated that before leaving the country he requested his Advocate to take steps for adjournment of hearing a statement which was not made in the application itself and which was rightly objected to. P.W.2, Mr. Syed Altaf Hossain learned advocate for the appellant in the trial Court does not say a word corroborating P.W.1 on this point. Therefore, we can safely come to the conclusion that the appellant left for U.S.A. without making any arrangement for conduct of the case on 16.7.80. There is nothing on record that he had to leave for U.S.A. suddenly or that he had no time to instruct his lawyer. P.W. 2 has stated that on 16.7.80 he flied an application for adjournment on the ground of his illness. No such application has been filed or marked as an exhibit and no such application is available in the case record either. P.W. 2 Mi. Syed Altar Hossain was engaged by the appellant from the beginning of the suit till the filing of the miscellaneous case and. therefore, it is absolutely unexplained as to what positive steps he took on 16.7.80 for the conduct of the case. The learned Subordinate Judge has found from the mere fact of the appellant's stay abroad that he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing. Mere absence from the country in the facts and circumstances of the case does not amount to a sufficient cause. In the background of the case history we are inevitably led to inquire as to whether the appellant made sufficient arrangement for conduct of the case on 16.7.80 or not. From the evidence on record we find that he did not and, therefore, we do not think mat he was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing on 16.7.80. The order-sheet dated 16.7.80 does not show that his lawyer prayed for any adjournment, far less on any ground of illness and his absence on that day and the absence of his lawyer cannot be explained. 

 17. On the second question as to whether the delay in filing the miscellanceous case should be condoned or not, we find that the petitioner returned LO the country on 7.9.80 and his only son died in an accident on 27.9.80. P.W.l says in his evidence that on return he contacted his Advocate who told him that the date of hearing was fixed sometime in the second week of September, 1980 and that he would inform the appellant the date of hearing in due time. There is no corroboration of this statement of P.W.l in the evidence of P. W.2 except that he made' a bland statement that on return to Bangladesh his client contacted him. 

 19. P.W. 2 Mr. Syed Altaf Hossain stated in his evidence that he found the next date of hearing of the suit on 18.K80 and on 28.9.80 he found the suit fixed for compromise. He checked up the matter on 29.9.80 and found to his dismay that he was pursuing the dates of Title Suit No. 322 of 1980 instead of Title Suit No. 322 of 1977 owing to inadvertence. It passes our understanding as to why P:W. 2 thereafter went after the record of Title Suit No. 322 of 1977, when in a matter of minutes he could check up the daily cause list to find out as to what happened to the Title Suit No. 322 of 1977 on 16.7.80. We are, therefore, not convinced at all that the entire period from 28.9.80 to 20.11.80 was consumed by P.W. 2 in the wild goose chase of the records of Title Suit No. 322 of 1977. This was a convenient excuse and we cannot accept that. 

 20. Finally, P.W. 2 stated that he came to know finally on 20.11.80 after search that the suit was decreed ex parte on 16.7.80. His client, P.W.l, was informed about the ex parte decree on 23.11.80. Thereafter it has not been explained at all why the miscellaneous case was filed on 20.12.80. A non-notified co-sharer under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act files an application for pre-emption from the date of his knowledge, but a person against whom an ex parte decree has been passed cannot borrow the analogy of section 96 and take upon himself an added advantage of another 30 days to file the miscellaneous case. This part of the delay is not explained at all anywhere.
